links.note: Models gap-junction blockade as reduced effective diffusion of AP/ML morphogen signals to produce altered planarian head shapes, the phenomenon this claim reports.
Implements Friston et al. (2015) variational free-energy minimisation in which cells sharing a generative model self-assemble the target form.
The active-inference model gives each cell an implicit model of its place in the target morphology, as the claim proposes.
Simulates the free-energy minimisation whose minimum is reached when each cell occupies its unique inferred place.
Implements the scrambled-face example the claim cites of cell collectives reaching an organ-level target morphology despite perturbation.
Cells in the simulation minimise variational free energy during morphogenesis and regeneration, the mechanism the claim asserts.
Implements the voxel-based evolutionary design pipeline of passive ectoderm and contractile cardiac cells that the claim says can design organisms built from frog cells.
Simulates the dorsal-inversion collapse of locomotion that the claim reports for inverted designs.
Implements AFPO evolution under phase-randomised actuation, the selection regime that the claim says evolved derandomizing shapes.
Simulates mechanical laceration and its closure, the self-repair the claim asserts.
Simulates Picasso tadpole craniofacial organs moving along abnormal paths to a normal froglet face, against Vandenberg et al. (2012) landmark tracking.
Implements voltage-gated gap junctions G_gj(DeltaV) coupled to membrane voltage, the mechanism by which the claim says rewritable bioelectric memories form.

The simulation implements a bioelectric V_mem polarity switch in which a transient physiological perturbation (ivermectin) converts genetically wild-type planarian regeneration from one-head to two-head (2H0T), the head-number switch the claim asserts.
Simulates bioelectric circuit states that store a two-headed target and persist across regeneration (cryptic two-headed memory).
Models the cryptic bistable bioelectric state in which regenerating fragments can flip between one and two heads.
Implements transient gap-junction blockade as a mechanism by which planarian fragments build other species' head shapes.
Includes Kriegman et al. (2021) kinematic self-replication of Xenobots from loose cells, the behaviour the claim asserts.
Simulates scrambled tadpole faces reaching the correct frog-face configuration by novel paths.
The excitable FitzHugh-Nagumo clock gated by density-dependent YAP is the Hubaud et al. (2017) mechanism by which isolated PSM cells stay quiescent and oscillate only as a collective.
Contrasts goal-directed closed-loop normalisation with an open-loop fixed-displacement model that fails, the error-reducing feedback the claim asserts.
Homeostatic error correction toward a stored bioelectric target-morphology setpoint is the closed-loop anatomical feedback the claim describes.

DITH sets each cell interfacial tension by cortical tension minus adhesion to the specific neighbour, so the tension depends on what the surface touches and drives germ-layer cell shape and sorting, as the claim asserts.

The model gives each cell boundary a surface tension that depends on what it touches (like cell, unlike cell or medium) and that tension determines cell and aggregate shape, as the Thompson claim asserts.
The audit's plaice weight-length analysis checks whether k = W/L^3 varies with length, signalling a change of form during growth.

Excess marginal growth of an initially flat sheet buckling into edge waves is a direct formalisation of Thompson's mechanism of folds arising from local differences in growth rate within a uniform sheet.

Planar differential growth rates within the wing-disc epithelium position its folds (uniform growth gives unpinned buckling), implementing Thompson's mechanism of folds from local growth-rate differences in a uniform sheet.
Organ-to-body (brain, heart) proportions changing with size are the data the audit uses to check that organ size bears no constant ratio to body size.
The audit fits differential relative growth (allometry) of parts against whole-body size, the per-part specific growth rates this claim asserts underlie morphology.
The audit refits Durbin's tadpole-tail regeneration tables to check Thompson's statement that regenerative velocity falls roughly as 1/T^2.
Fitting growth laws to the Durbin/Ellis regeneration curves checks that regeneration follows an ordinary lawful growth curve.
The audit fits a two-like-pole field to the aster and spindle rays of the dividing Cerebratulus egg, checking that the mitotic figure has the geometry of a bipolar field of force.
The audit fits Delaunay sphere, cylinder and unduloid composites to the meridional profiles of real Lagena and other unilocular tests, checking that these cells take constant-mean-curvature forms.

The Cellular Potts Hamiltonian assigns bond-energy surface tensions between cell types and medium, so sorting of the reaggregate proceeds by minimising interfacial area, the surface-tension mechanism Thompson proposes for the form of cell aggregates.
Junction-angle statistics on corneal endothelium, onion epidermis and Thompson's parenchyma figures check that cell walls meet three at a time near 120 degrees regardless of cell size.
The Lami force balance implements the relation between relative interface tensions and junction angles that this claim invokes, with tensions only inferred, not measured.

The vertex energy yields a regular hexagonal ground state under uniform tension and cell area, with Lewis-law departures from hexagons as cell sizes vary, implementing the claim that hexagons are regular only with equal cells and uniform forces.
Segmented human corneal endothelium is checked for the hexagonal tessellation that closely packed cells in full contact are claimed to form.
The audit compares plant tissue partitions and other aggregate partitions with least-area configurations, the minimal-partition rule this claim states.
The audit compares the radiate-concentric structure of Harting's calcospherites with natural analogues, including plaice otoliths, which this claim says share that structure.
Ray angles of Grantia triradiate spicules measured on SEM plates are checked against the 120-degree and unequal-tension cell-junction geometry this claim predicts.

Sumper phase separation deposits silica in the interstices between close-packed droplets to give hexagonal pore lattices, a direct formalisation of Thompson mechanism of silica collecting in grooves between packed surface vesicles (though for diatoms rather than radiolarians).
The audit fits logarithmic against Archimedean and power spirals to segmented Nautilus and Conus shells, checking that molluscan shell spirals are logarithmic.
The logarithmic helicospiral generator builds whorl breadths in geometric progression via W, but does not measure real Nautilus or ammonite whorls.
A log-spiral fit to the Nautilus whorl profile is equivalent to checking that successive whorl breadths form a geometric progression.
Radial segmentation of a sectioned Nautilus shell measures whorl expansion along radii (W_median) and compares log-spiral with Archimedean fits, testing geometric progression of whorl breadths.
Raup's parameters (expansion, distance from axis, translation, aperture shape) are a direct formalisation of Thompson's few growth factors fixing every turbinate shell form.
The fitted spiral constant (k and whorl expansion W) for Nautilus gives the constant angle this claim puts near 80 degrees.
Raup's D parameter and whorl expansion rate govern whether whorls separate, touch or overlap, implementing the growth-ratio explanation without specimen data.
Testing that successive fusulinid whorls stand in constant proportion is a test that spiral foraminiferal shells are logarithmic spirals.
Shi (2021) fusulinid half-whorl series are checked against Thompson's near-constant 1:1.5 whorl ratio, a spiral of about 86 degrees.
The script derives the constant chamber ratio from growth proportional to existing mass algebraically, without testing that mechanism on specimens.
Log-spiral fits to a real Ovis ammon skull photograph and Thompson's horn figures check that horns are continuous logarithmic spirals.
The audit measures the spiral angle of Ovis ammon (Thompson: about 75 degrees) and of the Capra figure (under 70 degrees), the values in this claim's series.
A log-spiral fit to a real mammoth tusk checks that teeth grown by unequal permanent accretion take logarithmic-spiral form.
The audit detects a rising (21,34) to (34,55) parastichy cascade in a real sunflower head, the size-dependent change in parastichy numbers this claim describes.

The magnetic-drop simulation produces Fibonacci parastichy pairs purely from physical repulsion and the plastochron ratio, formalising the Thompson view that Fibonacci phyllotaxis needs no selective explanation.
The audit fits the Preston ovoid family to measured profiles of real bird eggs (1389 auk/penguin eggs, 181 species), checking that eggs are prolate solids of revolution, never oblate.
The audit checks the internal consistency of Thompson's membrane equation p_n + T(1/r + 1/r') = P but not the oviduct-pressure cause.
Murray's minimum-work principle (Poiseuille pumping power plus vessel-volume cost) is the formalisation of Thompson's claim that vessels are arranged for minimum effort and minimum wall surface.
The minimum-work angle law implemented for retinal bifurcations predicts Roux's rules that small branches leave at near-right angles and large branches at small angles.
Murray's (1926b) minimum-work branching-angle optimum is the cos x = L/L' energy-loss-ratio angle rule the claim states.
Couples masticatory strain to osteogenic front growth so that suture interdigitation collapses under mechanical unloading, implementing strain as a direct growth stimulus.
The crocodilian skull mappings are a direct instance of the general claim that related forms map onto one another by simple Cartesian deformations.
Fitting a grid deformation from the Archaeopteryx pelvis to the Apatornis pelvis tests whether a simple Cartesian transformation relates the two forms.
Affine and thin-plate-spline grid fits between the Hyrachyus and Aceratherium skull diagrams (and allies) test whether a simple coordinate deformation relates related skulls.
The human-to-ape-and-dog skull net fits are an instance of the general claim that related forms differ by simple Cartesian transformations.
Leaf-outline morphometrics test whether lanceolate, ovate and cordate outlines are polar transforms about the basal node, set by the ratio of radial to tangential growth.
The Begonia instance checks that the two leaf halves are similar figures in the same radial system, which this claim attributes to unequal growth.
Coordinate transformations fitted between real Crocodylus porosus, C. acutus and Alligator skulls test whether a single harmonious deformation relates crocodilian skulls (Notosuchus is unavailable).
Human skulls are mapped onto chimpanzee and baboon skulls by a fitted net, checking that one continuous deformation, with roughly logarithmic increase of cell areas, relates them.

The TGF-beta activator / FGF-dependent inhibitor system destabilises the uniform state into condensations through diffusion-driven instability, with the unstable wavenumber setting 1-2-3 skeletal elements.
Runs a Gierer-Meinhardt activator-inhibitor reaction-diffusion PDE whose diffusion-driven instability produces the angelfish stripes and their insertion.
Implements a Schnakenberg GDNF-RET reaction-diffusion system whose homogeneous steady state undergoes a diffusion-driven (Turing) instability.
The simulation runs a two-species diffusion-driven-instability model to generate the predicted coat pre-pattern.
Implements the Murray Thomas substrate-inhibition kinetics that are diffusively unstable above a critical diffusion ratio d_c.
Runs the Schnakenberg two-species reaction-diffusion scheme including its Turing (diffusion-driven) instability regime alongside the Hopf limit cycle.
WNT short-range activator and DKK long-range inhibitor generate the placode lattice by diffusion-driven instability.
The Gray-Scott and Kondo-Asai simulations rely on diffusion-driven instability of a homogeneous state with unequal diffusivities, the mechanism the claim states.
Uses a reaction-diffusion morphogen model with gap-junction-mediated diffusion to account for planarian head patterning.
Accounts for proximodistal limb skeletal patterning by reacting and diffusing morphogens (plus haptotaxis), the hypothesis the claim states.
Accounts for Pomacanthus stripe pattern and stripe insertion on a growing skin purely by reacting and diffusing morphogens.
A reaction-diffusion system on the scale-border geometry generates the dorsal skin colour labyrinth, an instance of reaction-diffusion accounting for a biological pattern.
Uses a ligand-receptor reaction-diffusion mechanism to generate ureteric bud branching patterns, an instance of morphogen reaction-diffusion accounting for tissue pattern.
The simulation runs Kondo-Asai reacting and diffusing Turing morphogens to generate and double the Pomacanthus stripes, implementing the morphogen reaction-diffusion mechanism the claim proposes.
Accounts for the hair-follicle placode pattern by reacting and diffusing morphogens (WNT and DKK).
Runs Turing/Kondo-Asai reaction-diffusion morphogen models to generate angelfish stripes and boxfish spots, implementing the claim that reacting, diffusing morphogens account for pattern.

The FGF-SHH Turing model of palatal rugae changes ruga spacing under cyclopamine (broader) and FGF10/Sprouty perturbations (compacted), i.e. reaction parameters set the repeat spacing, though these phenotypes are seeded rather than checked against measured spacings.
Digit spacing is set by the Turing network parameters and modulated by a distal FGF/Hoxd gradient that lengthens the wavelength, implementing parameter-controlled Turing wavelength selection.

The simulation lowers the Turing digit wavelength via distal Hox/Gli3 dose at roughly constant autopod width, so digit number rises, the parameter-not-size spacing control the claim asserts, though Sheth digit-period data are not quantitatively checked.
The WNT/DKK reaction-diffusion pair sets follicle spacing from reaction and diffusion parameters, with secondary follicles inserted as the skin grows and Dkk1 overexpression changing follicle number.

The Kondo-Asai angelfish model sets stripe spacing by reaction and diffusion parameters, a direct implementation of Turing wavelength selection, though the claim is not checked against measured spacings.
The audit checks the spot spacing measured on 10 Holstein specimens against the wavelength a Turing reaction-diffusion model predicts, reporting a negative result.
Generates Rule 30 from a single black cell, reproducing the irregular pattern the claim describes.
Computes finite-horizon statistics of the Rule 30 center column (through t = 1024), checking the randomness claim directly, though over far fewer than a million steps.
Uses Douady-Couder's inhibitory-potential process, from which the 137.5 degree divergence emerges, implementing the claim that the golden angle results from a simple inhibition growth process.
Raup's W/D/T/S generator is a simple few-parameter growth model that spans the mollusc shell morphospace, formalising the claim without measuring real shells.
Implements Conus textile pigmentation as a one-dimensional cellular automaton (Rule 30, Meinhardt-Klingler), the line-by-line mechanism the claim proposes.

Produces the ocellated-lizard scale labyrinth with a Kondo-Asai activation-inhibition system reduced to a hexagonal outer-totalistic cellular automaton, the local-match/longer-range-oppose rule the claim proposes.
Generates leopard spots/rosettes and tail rings from a short-range activation, long-range inhibition reaction-diffusion prepattern, the mechanism the claim proposes for coat patterns.
Short-range melanophore-xanthophore repulsion with long-range support is a local-activation / longer-range-inhibition rule producing zebrafish stripes and the leopard spot-to-stripe morphospace.
The Kondo-Asai activator-inhibitor kinetics are a local-activation, longer-range-inhibition rule producing animal stripe pigmentation, which is the mechanism this claim proposes for coat patterns.
Reaction-diffusion with local activation and longer-range inhibition is the mechanism the claim proposes for animal spots and stripes, simulated here for fish skin.
Holstein coat spotting is checked against the activator-inhibitor coat-pattern mechanism Wolfram says produces animal spots, and the hypothesis is reported as not supported.
Runs block-frequency statistics on the Rule 30 center column, the quantity this claim asserts is statistically random.
